sentences.text: Qianshanornis rapax was an extinct predatory bird that lived in China during the Middle Paleocene.
This creature was smaller than the Eocene bird Strigogyps and possessed a hypertrophied, hyperextensible second toe with a claw similar to that of dromaeosaurid dinosaurs.
Scientists propose that the bird's enlarged second toe helped it pin down captured prey.
Based on condylar processes, Qianshanornis rapax was likely capable of flight and may have been a superior flier compared to Strigogyps or modern seriemas.

Mayr and colleagues classified Qianshanornis in the monotypic family Qianshanornithidae because the specimen differed from other cariamiform birds, though they considered it unlikely to be a gruiform.
Qianshanornis lived from 66 to 61.66 million years ago during the Danian stage.
Other researchers have questioned the relationship between Qianshanornis and cariamiform birds, considering its systematic affinities ambiguous.
